name: Acyclovir
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 800 mg orally every 4 hours, 5 times daily, for 7 to 10 days
200 mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily, for 10 days
400 mg twice daily for up to 12 months, then re-evaluate

key_interactions.effect: Raised acyclovir half-life and AUC and lowered urinary excretion and renal clearance (studied with IV acyclovir).
key_interactions.action: The label states the effect without a dose rule; account for it when kidney function is reduced.

common: Nausea and/or vomiting (2.7%, short-course genital herpes)
serious: Renal failure, in some cases fatal
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura/hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS) in immunocompromised patients
Neurologic reactions (confusion, hallucinations, seizure, encephalopathy; postmarketing)

monitoring: Kidney function (dose by creatinine clearance; renal failure reported)
Neurologic status in older adults and in kidney impairment

pk.half_life_eskd: Acyclovir about 14 hours in ESRD (measured after valacyclovir dosing; VALTREX label)
pk.dialyzability: Yes: half-life about 5 hours during hemodialysis; a 6-hour session lowers plasma levels by about 60%. PD: no supplemental dose after interval adjustment (label).

sources.citation: Atlantic Biologicals Corp.. (2026). Acyclovir suspension (acyclovir) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, ANDA217393, set ID 5105272f-cff8-8898-e063-6394a90aabb5, version effective May 4, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

GlaxoSmithKline LLC. (2025). Valtrex (valacyclovir) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA020487, set ID f8e0d8f8-cb73-4206-a484-88f5c4fbd719, version effective November 12, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: ESKD acyclovir half-life comes from the VALTREX (valacyclovir) US label, not the acyclovir label (which gives only the 5-hour on-dialysis value). Accept a sister-label source or blank the field.
Selected label is an oral suspension (ANDA); it has no numbered Warnings list and no PD clearance data.

Neurologic reactions are listed under postmarketing experience; the 'older adults and kidney impairment' monitoring line is a clinical inference from the label's geriatric/renal text. Confirm or delete.
Peak time, Vd and percent renal excretion are not in the stored label text: left blank.
